unit: hexagons of 1 km² (equal area; longitude and latitude, WGS 84)
name: Hexagon grid, 1 km² (map layer)
plain: A map layer of equal hexagons of 1 km² over the island, shaded by residents, housing units, buildings, land under buildings or residents in the flood area, to compare places below the barrio in one unit.
definition: hex_grid.geojson: 8,745 hexagons of 1 km² (6,887 with residents), each with p (residents, 2020 Census), h (housing units), b (buildings), bf (land under buildings, % of the hexagon) and pf (residents in FEMA's 1% annual chance flood area, % of the hexagon's residents). The hexagons add up to Puerto Rico's 3,285,874 residents, 1,598,159 housing units and 2,157,363 buildings.
geography: Hexagons over Puerto Rico, Vieques and Culebra

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with python hexgrid.py when the blocks, the building release or the flood areas change.

method: hexgrid.py lays the map's own equal-area hexagons (core/hexbin.js: a Lambert azimuthal equal-area projection centred on Puerto Rico, pointy-topped hexagons of exactly 1 km²) and counts in each the census blocks by their internal point and the building footprints by their point. A block is counted whole in one hexagon, so a count per hexagon is calculated, not spread: a large rural block puts all its residents in one hexagon. A block is in the flood area when its internal point is (exposure.py's rule). Equal area means a count per hexagon is also a density per km².
source_detail: 2020 Census blocks (TIGERweb layer 10); Overture Maps buildings, release 2026-10-21.0; FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer (flood.geojson)
how_to_read: Pick the measure under the layer. Because every hexagon is 1 km², the shades compare density directly. Read a single rural hexagon with care: a census block can be larger than a hexagon. The hexagons are not the FCC's H3 hexagons of the broadband layer, which vary in area.
caveats: A census block is counted whole in the hexagon of its internal point; a block that spans several hexagons puts all its residents in one.
Buildings include sheds and other small structures in the footprint data.
Residents in the flood area use FEMA's 1% annual chance area as published in flood.geojson (outlines simplified by about 5 m).
